finding: Exact component projection composes correctly under the declared variable-separation assumptions. In the constructed 64-problem stream, repeated local discovery fell from 512 to 8 templates, independently checked answers remained 64/64 and instrumented elapsed time was 4.355985 versus 0.500504 seconds. Renaming, unsupported updates and non-affine factors provide preserved failures.
limitations: Exact syntax matching does not recognize variable renamings efficiently; stress stream grows to 504 new cache entries.
Efficient global solving requires an efficiently composable family (affine here); arbitrary 3-SAT does not inherit this property.
Learning and verification can be exponential in unbounded component size.
An easy live update returned UNKNOWN; this is preserved, not hidden.
method: Exact existential projection theorem for disjoint private-variable interfaces; restricted affine-relation compilation, exact syntax cache, original-CNF certificate checking and independently executed verifier.
open_questions: Can a checked rename-invariant signature lower total end-to-end cost on held-out sequences?
Can exact reusable interfaces be discovered under new cross-component constraints without expensive regeneration?
